newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran papers say Gulf Arab criticism U.S.-dictated.
newsitem.headline: Iran papers say Gulf Arab criticism U.S.-dictated.

text.p: Iranian newspapers attacked Gulf Arab leaders on Tuesday for criticising the Islamic republic's armament programme and said the only threat to the oil-rich Gulf region came from the United States and Western powers.

They described as "American-dictated" a statement by leaders from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Kuwait and Qatar at the end of a summit in the Qatari capital Doha criticising Iran's military development programmes and deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the region.
The statement said Iran's programmes exceeded "conventional" defensive needs and called on international agencies to rid the oil-rich region of all weapons of mass destruction.

"...The leaders of the Persian Gulf, since the formation of their alliance in 1981, have been issuing anti-Iran statements which has now become a routine with no value or significance for the Islamic republic or for the people of the region," the English-language Iran News said.

The Tehran Times said: "The real threat to the throne of the Persian Gulf states comes from their subservience to Washington and diplomatic flirting with the Zionist regime (Israel). This has alienated the masses from the rulers in those countries."
"Iran is the main source of stability in the region. If there is no security for Iran, there cannot be security for any other state in the region," it added.

Kayhan International said: "The Arab rulers...should understand that the real danger does not come from the Iranian side. Iran has never posed any threat to the various sheikhdoms in the Persian Gulf region. The threats have always come from outside the region as well as from among the Arabs themselves."

Gulf Arab states had repeatedly accused Iran of posing a threat to the security of the region -- which has about half the world's proven oil reserves -- and accused it of interfering in the internal affairs of the region's countries.
